cohort: 100 women with prolonged pregnancy beyond 40 weeks gestation and a Bishop score of less than 6.
finding: Mifepristone had a modest effect on cervical ripening when given 24 hours prior to labor induction and appeared to reduce the need for misoprostol compared with placebo, with no statistically significant difference in perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: The mifepristone group showed a higher rate of vaginal delivery within 24 hours without augmentation (16% vs 4%) and lower rates of cesarean (12% vs 16%) and instrumental deliveries (4% vs 10%) compared to the placebo group.
